claims.statement: TermindPresentation contains reusable SwiftUI form and presentation types, while ArchitectureBoundaryTests forbids app, AppKit/UIKit, storage and RemoteInfrastructure imports there and separately restricts ListViewKit to approved native-list workloads.

TFM centralizes desktop geometry in Metrics, including shared sidebar sizing and row rhythm, separate split-divider visual/hit dimensions, card ranges and a common 840-point full-Assistant reading width.

TFM uses semantic AppKit-backed colors and appearance-resolved native colors. Generic Highlight retains its accent wash, while Sidebar selection uses neutral primary fills at 10% key/6% inactive opacity, primary selected key-window text and accent leading icons, secondary inactive foregrounds and readable inline rename colors; the native menu outline remains accent-colored.

TFM explicit glass controls use system glass on macOS 26 with native material fallbacks, but the Sidebar column relies on NavigationSplitView's own background on macOS 26+ and adds only a pre-26 AppKit visual-effect fallback. Mobile cards retain conditional glass, dense-text backing and opaque/stronger-border accessibility fallbacks.

Mobile cards use width-derived columns with accessibility sizes forcing one column, a 106-point minimum height and at most two visible tags; primary card taps and secondary context-menu actions differ from desktop managed selection/reordering machinery.

Shared Host organization, protocol-profile and connection fields bind to platform-owned Host drafts; desktop keeps nested editing in the Vault work column, while mobile presents a draft-backed editor sheet with its own route, dirty-state and save gate.

SingleLineTextInput normalizes newline runs only for user edits and preserves attributed paste content, leaving reads unchanged; native input/paste is delegated through app-supplied environment adapters rather than shared platform imports.

AssistantTranscriptEntry shares stable timeline-derived typed rows and caller-supplied edit/fork eligibility, while desktop cached native ownership and mobile native-list environment/update handling remain distinct platform concerns.

UI visibility gates also control interaction/accessibility, motion helpers expose Reduce Motion policy, and adaptive tests cover language variants, native identity, focus and marked-text preservation rather than only final strings.

Continuity uses different retention budgets: desktop parked workspace geometry, an unmounted-owner transcript LRU, mobile app-owned workspaces with background-expiration policy, and stable children in adaptive mobile region layouts.

Both apps consume binding-driven TerminalFontFields with the shared 8–36 editing range, using a macOS Slider and iOS Stepper. App-owned font catalogs include any family with a loadable monospaced member, sort in localized order and refresh on settings appearance or scene activation; unavailable family choices remain stored while rendering resolves a copy.

TerminalFontSettings stores typography locally through AppStorage, separately from synchronized TerminalPreferences; TerminalSettingsModel persists preference edits before publishing and retains existing preferences on a save failure while exposing storageError.

TerminalThemePicker retains missing, empty or wrong-appearance selection values with a localized hint while the renderer chooses an appearance-specific fallback without writing preferences. Rendering applies base theme, custom overlay and local typography in order; the base picker remains editable with overlays. Desktop custom editing autosaves and imports files, while mobile explicitly saves a draft sheet.

Focused terminal tests verify complete macOS monospaced-family membership, local-font precedence and controller identity, filtered theme catalogs and fallback, overlay/base interaction, and zero writes on presenting the actual desktop settings page; mobile font rendering tests cover English and both Chinese variants.

The Sidebar mode rail shares one glass capsule with neutral animated selection, explicit selected accessibility traits, Reduce Motion handling and key-window focus outline; the Assistant footer groups interactive New Chat/Archive glass controls on macOS 26+, using neutral Archive selection and a semibold primary glyph.

Desktop single-rule forwarding menus group Address and SSH Command in a Copy submenu, while mobile exposes flat copy actions before Edit/Duplicate; both use native pasteboards, disable unavailable SSH-command copying and leave forwarding execution to separate actions.

Desktop and mobile Snippet cards expose one Run action rather than a separate override; desktop fills empty saved target lists with a chooser and checks destructive multi-selection, while mobile filters saved targets to valid Hosts, chooses hosts if none remain and confirms destructive execution before calling its execute callback.

Mobile Host cards activate through scene routing on tap, while their context menu groups protocol-filtered SSH/Telnet/SFTP connection actions separately from Edit/Duplicate and destructive Delete; even a Host with no enabled protocol retains editing and deletion actions.

Host menu operations remain platform-owned: the mobile card delegates connection to its scene callback, editing to a sheet and deletion to confirmation; MobileAppModel duplicates with a new ID and removes Host-custom SSH, Telnet and proxy identity references (clearing proxy username with Host-custom proxy identity), while desktop HostContextMenu offers separate Quick Connect, Connect and Copy SSH Command actions.

MobileRootView binds the selected destination to a scene model and preserves one NavigationStack per registered feature inside a sidebar-adaptable TabView; adaptive tests assert the same native tab controller, five available tabs and scene/native selection with visible titles across compact and regular sizes and language/Dynamic Type variants.

MobileContentRegions subtracts active obstacles and uses a usable division only when both regions fit; MobilePaneLayout retains the same native children and last usable size while Assistant and Metrics gate obscured panels' hit testing and accessibility along with visibility.

Adaptive mobile tests verify native continuity beyond displayed strings: Metrics list identity, offset and selected page survive folds and vertical-menu transitions; Assistant transcript, composer focus and marked text survive divisions/occlusion; search, editor drafts and in-flight save feedback survive width changes.

MobileAppModel loads and prunes saved workspace descriptors on cold launch without reconnecting them, consolidating previous scene records into the first bound session; MobileWorkspaceSessionModel publishes a selected descriptor as a live workspace before connecting, reuses one already live in that session, removes missing-Host entries, and disconnects and removes saved rows on explicit close. Background expiration suspends live work and an active scene resumes it.

Desktop workspace layout drag retains the native source pane mounted but omits it from temporary geometry; a pre-mounted native receiver checks current displayed workspace and matching pasteboard identity before preview/drop, splitting occupied pane edges or replacing empty slots, and rejects hidden destinations and unrelated drags.

Desktop Navigator layout drops use a native overlay on the List and measured global row frames to clamp pointer positions to Workspace insertion boundaries; preview geometry includes the dragged row while the move index excludes it, and valid Navigator drops reorder a workspace or detach a pane.

Vault presents MobileHostEditor as an item-based sheet for new or existing Hosts; the editor seeds a local Host draft and uses the shared profile and connection fields while each platform supplies its own group and tag controls.

Mobile Host Save eligibility requires a nonblank address, an enabled terminal protocol, valid enabled ports, valid custom identity/proxy configurations and valid SSH environment variables; desktop additionally checks SFTP initial path and validated SSH route in its own policy.

The mobile Host's separate temporary custom-identity draft loads once when the editor appears; saving uses the Host library to persist custom identities and the Host, whereas child identity, group and environment-variable sheets feed selections or values back into the parent draft.

MobileEditorSheet owns mobile form navigation and save lifecycle: dirty Cancel confirms discard, an in-flight save disables editing and interactive dismissal, success dismisses, and failure displays an error without dismissing.

Desktop Find resolves a foreground destination or focused workspace pane to the owning query, leaving Welcome's search in content and Settings or unsearchable workspaces without titlebar Find; macOS 26 uses a system searchable toolbar item while older macOS uses a native field with an owner and direct focus handler to protect keyboard intent during toolbar replacement, with terminal find navigation and cancellation on both paths.

Desktop toolbar creation actions derive from the foreground destination rather than sidebar mode, with the same page-specific verbs available as Navigator row native menu entries without first navigating to that page.

AgentToolPresentation projects human-readable summaries and details without modifying execution/replay data: approval displays in-memory unredacted request arguments only for live review, MCP output retains remote-defined presentation, failed knowledge results bypass success presenters, and bounded previews keep full transformed text available for desktop native Copy.

Mobile card tests verify measured card-height stability across tag counts, width-dependent columns and accessibility one-column layout; opt-in serialized mobile toolbar tests verify save, failure and cancel behavior across localized labels.

Shared AppStrings owns on-demand localized presentation resources for both apps; SwiftUI's swiftUIKey bridge preserves interpolation metadata, while AppLocalization resolves resources for native copy against a requested locale and app-bundle localization. Architecture tests reject app-local AppStrings declarations and presentation-copy tests cover English and two Chinese scripts.

The desktop Settings index offers App, Notifications, Terminal, Connections, AI and Sync category routes (Developer only in DEBUG); Logging is a separate optional debug entry, and Pro opens the paywall without adding a Settings category.

Desktop SettingsRoute defines a parent hierarchy: category and Logging lead to index, AI detail routes lead to AI except provider models which lead back to the provider, and terminal configuration leads to Terminal. Toolbar Back walks this hierarchy and then restores the window destination; if the displaced workspace no longer exists, it falls back to Vault.

On desktop SettingsPageView handles route-change and disappearance cleanup of provisional AI drafts: empty unconfigured providers are discarded outside provider/model-list transitions, new MCP servers require a valid draft and lockable namespace, while a skill with written content is retained as a draft. This policy remains in the app-owned Settings route rather than shared form fragments.

Mobile Settings uses a registered scene-owned tab with its own NavigationStack and native category NavigationLinks; the mobile paywall is a sheet controlled by app pro state rather than a desktop SettingsRoute destination.

Confirmation dialog titles should pass LocalizedStringResource directly instead of the swiftUIKey bridge, because UIKit-backed presentations can expose interpolated locale metadata; ArchitectureBoundaryTests scans both apps for bridged AppStrings confirmation titles.

The mobile snippet view defers final execution to an injected callback after target choice and risk confirmation, while MobileWorkspaceSessionModel's execution path creates one SSH workspace per permitted host with the snippet command carried only by live workspace startup, not its restoration descriptor.

Mobile workspace scene disconnection does not itself discard restorable sessions; native open-session reconciliation identifies orphan sessions and recovers their live workspaces and saved descriptors into the active session only after the merged snapshot is persisted successfully.

Both app settings shells expose NotificationSettingsFields for notification permissions and configuration, supplying the platform-specific open-settings action while maintaining independent desktop route and mobile native link navigation.

When cold-launch workspace descriptor consolidation fails to persist, MobileAppModel reports a restoration error and fences further session binding from claiming the same previous-scene records twice.
